features.title: Local Privacy Proxy & Sanitization Engine
features.user_visible_behavior: A startup operator can pipe raw log/feedback text through the local proxy and receive a sanitized, PII-free structural metadata object — with all emails, names, phone numbers, API keys, and JWT tokens stripped before any data leaves the local process.
verification: Feed a sample log containing synthetic PII (email, phone, API key, JWT) into the proxy.
Assert all PII patterns are absent in the output.
Assert the output contains only structural metadata (field names, data types, event frequencies).
Confirm no outbound HTTP call is made during processing (network intercept / mock).
Run the unit test suite for the sanitization module.
evidence: TestSanitizerOutput::test_output_contains_no_raw_pii PASSED — no PII values in metadata output
All PII types verified: email, phone, JWT, AWS key, Stripe SDK key, IPv4, generic api_key
features.notes: Uses regex + local NER (spaCy en_core_web_sm). NER degrades gracefully if model not downloaded. spaCy model not yet installed — NER entity counting will activate once 'python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm' is run. All core verification passes without it.

features.title: AI PM Triage Matrix & Relaxation Control Dashboard
features.user_visible_behavior: A CTO can view their anonymized backlog ranked by Severity / Friction / Sensitivity, see Red/Yellow/Green sensitivity tags, and use the Relaxation Controls (abstract logic toggle, variable-name synthesizer, noise slider) to safely de-risk an issue before publishing it as a public challenge.
verification: Load three sample anonymized metadata blobs into the triage dashboard.
Verify each item renders a Severity, Friction, and Sensitivity score.
Verify Red/Yellow/Green tag is displayed correctly based on sensitivity score.
Toggle 'Abstract Proprietary Logic' and confirm the preview panel updates.
Adjust the noise slider to 50% and confirm the synthesized dataset distribution shifts.
Confirm no raw metadata is sent to external APIs before the founder approves a challenge.
features.notes: LLM call receives only the anonymized structural metadata produced by privacy-001. See PRD Feature 2.

features.title: Public Sandbox Terminal & Micro-PRD Framework
features.user_visible_behavior: A student can browse published challenges, read a Micro-PRD (Context, Definition of Success, Structural Constraints, Sandbox Instructions), download a synthetic dataset, and write/run code in an interactive terminal within the browser.
verification: Publish a sample challenge from the triage dashboard.
Open the challenge as a student — verify the Micro-PRD renders all four sections.
Download the synthetic dataset and confirm it contains the injected anomalies (nulls, index bottleneck, unoptimized join).
Submit a minimal working solution via the terminal.
Confirm the submission is received by the assessor layer.
features.notes: Synthetic dataset generated by the procedural noise engine seeded from the relaxed metadata. See PRD Feature 3.

features.title: AI Assessor & Taste-and-Judgment Scorecard
features.user_visible_behavior: After a student submits a solution, the AI Assessor runs it against secret edge-case tests in an ephemeral sandbox, evaluates code taste (error handling, architectural simplicity, optimization), and renders a dynamic scorecard. Top profiles are surfaced to the sponsoring company dashboard.
verification: Submit two solutions to a sample challenge — one well-structured, one naive.
Verify both run inside an isolated container with no network access and enforced memory/CPU limits.
Verify the scorecard shows distinct scores for 'Performance', 'Security Resilience', and 'Architectural Elegance'.
Verify the well-structured solution scores higher on taste metrics.
Confirm the top-performing candidate profile appears in the sponsoring company's matching radar.
features.notes: Code runner uses Docker ephemeral containers. LLM evaluates taste after test execution. See PRD Feature 4.
